title: Example budget from polynomial bounds
statement: Fix $k,d,e\in\mathbb{N}$ and suppose there is a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $n,b\in\mathbb{N}$, the uniform node random-example bound at per-call failure parameter $2^{-(b+1)}/T_k$ is at most $C(n+1)^d(b+1)^e$, where $T_k$ is the junta-tree call count. Then, as $n$ and $b$ tend jointly to infinity, the total random-example budget at failure parameter $2^{-(b+1)}$ is $O\!\left((n+1)^d(b+1)^e\right)$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural-number constant $C$ bounds the uniform node random-example count by $C(n+1)^d(b+1)^e$ for every $n,b\in\mathbb{N}$ at per-call failure parameter $2^{-(b+1)}/T_k$
